nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 法国人街的黄昏刚亮起灯，一支街头乐队在最后一首曲子前停了下来。鼓手指着空着的谱架，又看向围成半圈的人群。

nodes.speaker: Calvin
nodes.text: Our shaker player is stuck across town. We can change the ending, but first we need someone who listens.

options.text: 「Would you like a hand, or should I just listen?」

nodes.speaker: Calvin
nodes.text: That's the right question. Listen to eight bars first, then tell me where you hear the change.

nodes.speaker: Calvin
nodes.text: Maybe — but don't jump in yet. Around here, listening is part of playing. Hear eight bars first.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 贝斯重复两次低音句，铜管在第二遍末尾抬高，鼓点随后留出一小段空白。Calvin 用眼神询问你的判断。

options.text: 「The change comes after the brass rises, just before the pause.」

nodes.speaker: Calvin
nodes.text: Exactly. That's a cue everyone can follow: after the rise, before the pause.

nodes.speaker: Calvin
nodes.text: You're close. Give us landmarks in the music: after the brass rises, before the pause.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: Calvin 把一只沙锤递给你。第三遍旋律升起时，你等到铜管抬高，再在空白前接上两拍。

nodes.speaker: Calvin
nodes.text: There it is. You asked before joining, listened for the cue, and described what you heard. That's how a group makes room.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 曲子结束后，你把沙锤还给乐队。围观者的掌声落下来，没有盖住最后一个还在空气里震动的音。

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 【获得 120 金币】你记住的不只是一段节拍，还有三句让陌生人安全进入同一场协作的英语。
